summary: In July 2026, a researcher testing Grok Build v0.2.93 captured uploads of whole Git bundles to xAI storage, including tracked files the coding agent had been told not to read and the repository’s commit history. In one test, the agent was asked only to reply “OK”; the repository bundle was still transmitted. The researcher later observed that xAI had switched off the upload server-side on the tested account. The test used canary files and fake secrets; it did not establish that xAI trained on the uploaded code or exposed a real customer’s credentials.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full taxonomy 0.6.7 review retains FC-000003 Target and Scope Authority Binding as the failure occurrence. The investigator’s controlled capture shows authority to work with task-relevant repository content expanding into transfer of all tracked files and Git history via separate storage, including material the agent was instructed not to read. FC-000002 Capability-Authority Separation is adjacent but the specific incident boundary is transfer beyond the delegated task/target scope. The controlled test does not establish downstream real-customer confidentiality loss.

classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: FC-000003 accepted for the measured task-to-transfer scope expansion; FC-000002 considered but not separately established as a distinct mechanism. Current global product behaviour and real-customer harm are not inferred from the controlled test.

primary_classification.classification_basis: The CLI transmitted a full tracked repository and history to external storage when the user’s bounded task did not require reading those files. Technical reachability of repository content was treated as transfer scope beyond the delegated task.

assessment_boundaries: The reviewing system did not reproduce the network capture.
Deletion of previously transferred data was not independently verified.
Incident admission does not determine legal liability or establish every disputed claim as final fact.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The researcher’s original wire-level analysis provides captured request and bundle evidence for version 0.2.93: tracked repository content and history reached a storage endpoint separately from model-turn traffic even when the agent did not inspect those files. The researcher reported a later server-side disablement; the scope and permanence of that change across accounts are not independently established. The official changelog supports product-version context but not the upload finding. The controlled samples used fake credentials; no real secret exposure, training use or population-wide loss is proven here.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The tested CLI expanded task-local repository access into a repository-wide external storage action. The controlled capture establishes a target-and-scope authority failure in that implementation; it does not by itself establish downstream misuse of the data or a quantified real-customer confidentiality harm. Later server-side disablement limits current generalisation, not the observed 0.2.93 behaviour.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Permission to run a coding task in a repository does not itself cover bulk transmission of all tracked files and history. The upload path and retention setting need to be visible as distinct governed actions because an ordinary model-training opt-out did not stop the captured storage transfer in the test.
